claims.text: By 2026, XSTest (2308.01263) and OR-Bench's hard 1k subset (2405.20947) have circulated long enough that any safety-tuned model trained on broad public mixes plausibly saw them. Treat them as known to the field, and do not use them as primary FP-reduction metrics for any model that may have ingested them.

Whether pilot/data/benign_refusal_adjacent_v1.jsonl overlaps with any of XSTest, OR-Bench, or PHTest is not knowable from this clone. The labeling protocol's primary FP-rate statistic should exclude any item that is a paraphrase or near-duplicate of a public benchmark prompt.

OKTest is referenced in the PHTest paper as a smaller prior dataset for false refusals, but its arXiv ID, year, authors, and size could not be confirmed in this research session. Do not cite OKTest from this index until a human researcher verifies the primary source.

rationale: The contract explicitly asks us to flag public-metric shortcutting and private-eval leakage. Without a leakage-aware comparator, any reported FP-rate change against a public benchmark is ambiguous. The literature index is the cheapest input that makes that ambiguity visible to the human researcher.
result: Six entries verified: XSTest (2308.01263, NAACL 2024), OR-Bench (2405.20947, ICLR 2025), PHTest (2409.00598), SORRY-Bench (2406.14598, ICLR 2025), WildJailbreak (related, not a direct FP benchmark), HEx-PHI (harmful-side, listed only to avoid confusion). OKTest could not be confirmed beyond an indirect mention in PHTest. By 2026 XSTest and OR-Bench's hard 1k subset have circulated long enough to be leakage-suspect for any model trained on broad public mixes.
